note: ORPHAN Pro 26:13 — the sluggard says, 'there is a lion in the road! a lion in the streets!'

dims.v: evasive sloth — inventing lions in the road to avoid going out
the sluggard who says 'there is a lion in the road!' — sloth conjuring imaginary perils to excuse staying in, laziness so inventive that it peoples the streets with lions rather than step out to work
(the imagined lion that keeps him in)
the idleness that invents dangers rather than face the day's work

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD says, 'there is a lion in the road!'' (26:13; cf 22:13); sloth excuses itself with fantastic fears. The lazy man sees lions where none are, sooner than admit he simply will not work.
